title: Prioritising goals: must, should, nice-to-have
objectives: Sort goals into must-have, should-have and nice-to-have, and fund in that order.
body_md:
Must-have: retirement, children's education — fund first; protect with the right asset mix. Should-have: house, car upgrade — fund next; dates can flex. Nice-to-have: foreign holiday, second home — fund with what's left; adjust freely.

| Priority | Examples | How to treat it |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Must-have | Retirement, children's education | Fund first; protect with the right asset mix |
| Should-have | House, car upgrade | Fund next; dates can flex |
| Nice-to-have | Foreign holiday, second home | Fund with what's left; adjust freely |

A common conflict: parents often put children's education above their own retirement. A useful reminder: education can be part-funded by a loan; retirement cannot.
example: A couple funding an MBA in 12 years and retirement in 20: quantify both with inflation, prioritise, and discuss the education-loan vs retirement trade-off openly.
say: Fund must-haves first; dates for should-haves can flex.
Education can be part-funded by a loan; retirement cannot.
never: Fund goals in order of excitement.
Parents should always fund education before retirement.
